item.title: Re: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded: You know what's really creepy? Real-world extortionists. A friend had his Bitcoin wallet dust attacked, like a million bucks on the address. OP_Return message: I see you. Reads like an SCP. this is real life. Anyone can be exposed on the internet, which is frightening. So why do these perpetrators have to be ET? ET raised more questions than it answers, in a not great, sort of cliched way, while mystery about these incidences may be more effective.

item.title: Re: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Okay so I have two big concerns here. The first is that narratively, it feels like this is very similar to SCP-4645 in style; down to the like, random blackmail claims and the unclear like, requirement for what the foundation should do.

The second is that this doesn't really go anywhere: you introduce the mystery of who is sending this and that the blackmail changes repeatedly but it doesn't go anywhere. Like, the foundation doesn't investigate who sent it, they don't really debate whether to accede to the demands, they don't refuse and have progressively worse things happen; so it just feels very…flat?

My advice: figure out how you can show why this is interesting. Figure out what the narrative arc of this is.

item.title: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Mystery

Page Layout: Scp article with story elements

Elevator Pitch

  • A blackmail envelope listing demands by the threat of release of information about the secret it is unknown what this secret is and its severity.
  • It gives a negative feeling when it appears within a 10-meter radius to all sentient organisms there has been no found pattern to the negative feelings portrayed.
  • This blackmail appears and disappears and changing the demands between the period of absence via striking out the previous demands. Blackmail event
+ show block
– hide block

central narrative:
The following message is inscribed in the blackmail at the moment of Discovery:

Thank you kind soul for Believing in our case every dollar counts into our only goal to help the world be a more equal place where we don't have to worry about suppression and harassment with your help.

Look let's be real for a minute nobody cares about the idea of freedom and equality every person I have come across would ignore freedom even if it was right in front of their damn noses, so you are going to help me keep this going by giving $10 to meus,weI will tell everybody the secret, and Dr.[[REDACTED]] started cheating on his wife last week just wanted to let you know.
address to charity: go to your nearest charity
Contact information- 435-845-732
charityEvent#moc.liamg|3#moc.liamg|3
Contact through the phone number has yielded in an unidentified voice saying "thank you for Calling but I am kinda in a pickle so maybe we can talk later?
Hook/Attention Grabber: The secret is mysterious.

Additional Notes: The material used for writing the blackmail is mundane black ink, The blackmail disappearance and reappearance interval lasts 1-hour and it changes the kind of currency it wants to be used and the amount.

When you go to your nearest charity and use the correct kind of currency with the right amount of money you state with the intention of donating the charity stated in the blackmail when done correctly a blackmail event happens and the money disappears.

When the envelope is destroyed after 24 hours a bright red envelope which is impervious to damage in this state appears, but with double the demands, it reverts back to its normal state with a bright flash. inside it, there is a note stating: Why don't you slip into something more comfortable — like a coma?
.
